top_news.title: DeepSeek Harness Desktop for macOS and Windows
top_news.dek: DeepSeek has launched an open-source desktop client for macOS and Windows to interface with its models.
top_news.brief: The DeepSeek Harness desktop app is now in public preview, supporting everyday tasks and coding workflows. The project is open-source and features a plugin architecture, allowing developers to extend functionality. It is available for download on Apple Silicon and 64-bit Windows.

top_news.title: Reverse Item Response Theory for Sparsity-Robust Ranking in Fragmented Cancer Drug-Response Matrices
top_news.dek: Researchers apply reverse Item Response Theory to pharmacogenomics to rank cancer drug sensitivity.
top_news.brief: By modeling cancer types as subjects with resistance traits and drugs as items with evasion difficulty, this approach addresses sparsity in fragmented drug-response datasets. The model provides a robust ranking system for drug activity across diverse cancer types.
top_news.image_alt: Diagram showing latent trait modeling for drug-response matrices

top_news.title: Uber Eats Rebuilds Search Pipeline to Cut End-to-End Latency by 50%
top_news.dek: Uber Eats reduced search latency by 50% through pipeline re-engineering and infrastructure optimization.
top_news.brief: The overhaul included parallel hydration, redesigned advertising data, and reduced retrieval overhead. The team is now exploring advanced techniques like microbatching and HTTP multipart streaming to further improve performance.
top_news.image_alt: Chart showing latency reduction in search pipeline

top_news.title: Anthropic: Claude-shaped science
top_news.dek: Professor Matthew Schwartz introduces BootLoops, a toolkit for AI-assisted quantitative science.
top_news.brief: By focusing on 'Claude-shaped' problems—tasks specifically suited to LLM strengths—Schwartz developed a framework for exact calculations. The tool identifies cross-disciplinary connections, applying similar mathematical structures to fields ranging from ecology to population genetics.
top_news.image_alt: Conceptual illustration of AI-assisted scientific research

top_news.title: AI Gateway, Web Search API - Introducing Web Search API
top_news.dek: Cloudflare launches a beta Web Search API for AI agents to ground responses in real-time data.
top_news.brief: The API integrates with AI Gateway and supports providers including Ceramic.ai, Exa, and Linkup. All providers offer Zero Data Retention and adhere to verified bot crawling standards, enabling developers to bypass training cutoffs.
top_news.image_alt: Cloudflare Web Search API architecture diagram

primary.summary: We introduce reverse Item Response Theory (IRT) to pharmacogenomic drug-response analysis by treating cancer types as latent "subjects" with resistance ability and drugs as "items" with evasion difficulty. Applied to 242,036 drug sensitivity measurements from the Genomics of Drug Sensitivity in Cancer (GDSC2) database, the model estimates cancer-type-level in-vitro resistance and drug-level broad activity on a shared latent scale. primary.title: Workers AI - Introducing Clef: Cloudflare's first open-source decision models, now on Workers AI
primary.summary: Meet @cf/cloudflare/clef and @cf/cloudflare/clef-flash, the first models trained by the Cloudflare Workers AI team, available on Workers AI today. Clef is a decision model, in the same family as Typesafe's Jev ↗︎. Instead of generating text, it reads an input state and a set of typed questions, then returns a probability for every allowed answer. Your agent gets a structured decision it can act on immediately, for example: route the ticket, block the request, or escalate to a human. There is no free-form output to parse and no reasoning tokens to wait for. Both models are hosted on Workers AI
